A Windows optional feature, as DISM names it, such as TelnetClient or Microsoft-Windows-Subsystem-Linux. It never reboots: reboot_required says whether Windows wants one, and windows_reboot does it.

Use `windows_optional_feature` to turn a Windows optional feature on or off, such as the Telnet client, .NET Framework 3.5 or the Windows Subsystem for Linux. These are the features DISM lists, on desktop and server editions alike. Server roles and features, such as `Web-Server`, are [`windows_feature`](/modules/windows_feature).

## Example usage

```hcl
step "telnet" {
  windows_optional_feature {
    name = "TelnetClient"
  }
}
```

.NET 3.5 from install media, with a reboot only if Windows asks for one:

```hcl
step "netfx3" {
  windows_optional_feature {
    name           = "NetFx3"
    include_parent = true
    source         = "D:\\sources\\sxs"
  }
}
```

```hcl
step "restart_if_needed" {
  windows_reboot {
    only_if_pending = true
  }
}
```

## Arguments

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `include_parent` | bool | No | Also enable the features this one sits under, as -All does. |
| `name` | string | Yes | Feature name, as Get-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online lists it, such as TelnetClient. |
| `source` | string | No | Where DISM finds the feature's files when Windows doesn't have them, such as D:\sources\sxs or a share. |
| `state` | string | No | "present" (default) or "absent". |
| `timeout` | string | No | How long to allow. Defaults to "30m". |

## Read-only attributes

Conn3x sets these; reference them as `conn3x_windows_optional_feature.<circuit>__<step>["<host>"].<name>`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `in_sync` | bool | Whether the feature matched at the last refresh. |
| `reboot_required` | bool | Whether Windows reported wanting a reboot after the last change. |
| `revision` | string | Changes each time Conn3x changes this on the host. Handlers watch it. |

A step lowers to the `conn3x_windows_optional_feature` resource, one instance per host, and connects with its circuit's `ssh` block.

## How it works

**Reading.** On every plan, Conn3x reads the feature with `Get-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online`. With `state = "present"`, `in_sync` is true when it's `Enabled`, or `EnablePending`, waiting for a reboot. With `"absent"`, it's true when it's `Disabled`, `DisablePending` or `DisabledWithPayloadRemoved`. So a change waiting for a reboot plans clean the second time. A name Windows doesn't list fails the plan.

**Applying.** Conn3x runs `Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature`, with `-All` when `include_parent` is true and `-Source` when `source` is set, or `Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature`. A `source` folder or share that isn't there fails before DISM runs, saying so. A `wim:` or `esd:` source, which names an image and its index, such as `wim:D:\sources\install.wim:1`, goes to DISM as it is. It always passes `-NoRestart`, then reads the feature back. Windows servicing takes one change at a time, so Conn3x runs one `windows_feature` or `windows_optional_feature` change per host at a time. `timeout` defaults to `30m`.

**Reboots.** The step never reboots. `reboot_required` is true when Windows said the change needs one. A [`windows_reboot`](/modules/windows_reboot) step with `only_if_pending = true` after it reboots only then.

## Removal

Deleting a `windows_optional_feature` step leaves the feature as it is. To turn it off, set `state = "absent"`.

## From Ansible

`conn3x convert ansible` turns `ansible.windows.win_optional_feature` tasks into `windows_optional_feature` steps, a step for each `name` in the list. `state`, `include_parent` and `source` carry across. Ansible's task result has `reboot_required`, and so does the step, so a play that reboots when it's set can use a `windows_reboot` step with `only_if_pending = true` instead.
